market_context: US markets reopen for a half-day session (closes 1 PM ET) after Thanksgiving. Futures are sharply higher: S&P 500 up about 1.5-1.8%, Nasdaq-100 up about 2-2.8%, and Dow up about 1.3%. The move is a dip-buy rebound in beaten-down AI and chip stocks after Wednesday's intraday drop of as much as 3.2%. Risks are a likely Fed rate hike in December, a 10Y yield near 4.85-4.9%, Middle East oil tensions (Brent about $91-97), and analysts calling the bounce tactical.

predictions.reasoning: S&P futures are up about 1.5-1.8% pre-market against the 716.70 SPY baseline, which implies a gap-up open near 727-729. I expect some fade in a thin half-day session, since analysts call the rebound technical. The close should still finish well above the baseline.
Nasdaq-100 futures are up about 2-2.8% on a chip and AI rebound, with year-end seasonality and light volume helping. I allow for partial giveback from the opening gap, as AI stocks did on Wednesday.

NVDA is up about 2-4% pre-market after falling 3.9% on Wednesday and 5.9% on Tuesday, as semiconductor stocks lead the rebound (MU up about 6%). Volatility remains high after the CEO saga, so I expect the gain to hold only in part.

AMZN fell 3.1% on Wednesday and 8.7% over five days, and is among the mega-cap tech names rallying pre-market. A broad Nasdaq gap-up of about 2% should lift it, and oversold bounces often hold in holiday sessions.
MSFT is down 3.4% over five days and fell 1.25% on Wednesday, so it should follow the Nasdaq-100 futures gain of about 2% or more. Rising rate-hike odds and a 4.9% 10Y yield limit how far it can run.
